issue_context.title: pod created failed when devices resource request is 0
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

1 create deployment by yaml below
```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: jktest
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      workload.es.io: jktest
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        workload: jktest
    spec:
      containers:
      - image: centos:latest
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        name: test
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: 250m
            memory: 512Mi
            nvidia.com/gpu: "0"
          requests:
            cpu: 250m
            memory: 512Mi
            nvidia.com/gpu: "0"
```

2 create pod failed, the reason is 

```
status:
  message: >-
    Pod Node didn't have enough resource: nvidia.com/gpu, requestd: 0, used: 1,
    capacity: 0
  phase: Failed
  reason: OutOfnvidia.com/gpu
  startTime: '2022-02-02T12:40:19Z'  
```

node resource info 

```
...
allocatable: 
  memory: 252717800Ki       
  nvidia.com/gpu: "0"
  pods: "255"
capacity: 
  memory: 263278312Ki 
  nvidia.com/gpu: "0" 
  pods: "255"
...
```

### What did you expect to happen?

expect the pod create success, the request resource is 0, and it must not exceed

so it failed by somewhere unreasonable judgment

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1 create pod `a` which use hot pluggable device in resource.request, and the resource is 1
2 remove device
3 create pod `b` which use hot pluggable device in resource.request, and the ressource is 0

### Anything else we need to know?

comments: /sig scheduling
Why you set `nvidia.com/gpu` as `0`, if you don't want to request the resource.

> Why you set `nvidia.com/gpu` as `0`, if you don't want to request the resource.

I think so, but it is legal even if set resource `nvidia.com/gpu` as `0`. 

device `nvidia.com/gpu` is  hot plugging. and more magical is the device  was removed when pod is running which is using, and create another pod which set resource is `0` at once.
thus lead to `nodeInfo.Allocatable.ScalarResources[rName] - nodeInfo.Requested.ScalarResources[rName]` is negative number

Thanks. I may understand the problem you faced here. There is indeed a problem. The pod which is set `nvidia.com/gpu` as `0` is rejected by `kubelet` just because of out of the `OutOfnvidia.com/gpu`.  I think it's better to fix it in that part of the `kubelet` rather than in `scheduler`.

> 1 create pod a which use hot pluggable device in resource.request, and the resource is 1
2 remove device
3 create pod b which use hot pluggable device in resource.request, and the ressource is 0

IIUC, when we remove the device, `nodeInfo.Allocatable.ScalarResources[rName]` is 0, but `nodeInfo.Requested.ScalarResources[rName]` is still 1, right? If so, when we remove the device, we should update the requested values.

> 

actuall yes, if the `pod.spec.containers[1].resource.request.{resource}` not  set, the Pod will create successed. but when set the value is `0`, the Pod will create failed. 

IMO, it is little bug, and mostly should delete `request.resource`  in spec when the resource not use.

> > 1 create pod a which use hot pluggable device in resource.request, and the resource is 1
> > 2 remove device
> > 3 create pod b which use hot pluggable device in resource.request, and the ressource is 0
> 
> IIUC, when we remove the device, `nodeInfo.Allocatable.ScalarResources[rName]` is 0, but `nodeInfo.Requested.ScalarResources[rName]` is still 1, right? If so, when we remove the device, we should update the requested values.

Misunderstanding here, we may not update the requested values for first created pod is still requesting.
Maybe the patch https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/111544 is enough.

@yylt when the device is removed, does kubelet immediately remove pod `a`? If not, `a` would end up with requesting a non-existent GPU resource. Furthermore, this may lead to a more general issue: suppose a node has 4 GPUs, and a pod requests for 3 GPUs and gets scheduled. Let's say the 3 GPUs get unplugged, but the pod doesn't get deleted, in scheduler's cache, it reads GPU as 3(requested)/1(total) instead of 3/4. Then if an upcoming pod requests for 1 GPU, it will also fail the scheduling - this is a more critical issue that needs kubelet's changes if not today.

In terms of tolerating 0-requested req in scheduler, it's a good-to-have and not a root fix to this issue.

> Maybe the patch https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/111544 is enough.

I'd hold that as that won't "fix" this issue.

> @yylt when the device is removed, does kubelet immediately remove pod `a`? If not, `a` would end up with requesting a non-existent GPU resource. Furthermore, this may lead to a more general issue: suppose a node has 4 GPUs, and a pod requests for 3 GPUs and gets scheduled. Let's say the 3 GPUs get unplugged, but the pod doesn't get deleted, in scheduler's cache, it reads GPU as 3(requested)/1(total) instead of 3/4. Then if an upcoming pod requests for 1 GPU, it will also fail the scheduling - this is a more critical issue that needs kubelet's changes if not today.
> 
> In terms of tolerating 0-requested req in scheduler, it's a good-to-have and not a root fix to this issue.

good catch.

Now, memory and cpu is the same type, so could check quota by `Allocatable`. 
But when check quota on the hot plugged device, it is not enough, also should check `kubelt_internal_checkpoint` file to make sure have enough devices. Just because this is hot plugged device.

`available` cannot be a negative number. So if `rQuant` > `available`, `rQuant`  must be larger than `0`.
So `&& rQuant != 0` is useless.
